blockers.title: A held RPM descriptor fixes pathname replacement but does not freeze archive bytes across digest, verification, and extraction
evidence: preferredApi opens publisherArchivePath read-only and keeps one descriptor, but publisherArchivePath has no ownership, mode, mount, lease, seal, or immutable-snapshot requirement. A held descriptor pins an inode against rename; it does not prevent another writable handle from changing that inode's bytes.

The preferred sequence computes one sha256 during digest and then runs verify and extract later. descriptorConsumptionRecord retains that one digest plus a list of stage names, but no operation seals the file or proves the bytes seen during verify and extract equal the digest-stage bytes. No post-stage hash would exclude a mutate-use-restore execution unless writes are prevented during each child/library read.

The CLI copy is explicitly opened O_RDWR and the parent keeps that writable file description. Directory mode 0700 and file mode 0600 exclude other UIDs, not every process with observerProcessIdentity's UID, and no writable-descriptor closure or F_SEAL_WRITE/F_SEAL_GROW/F_SEAL_SHRINK equivalent is required. Immediately-before and post-exit fstat compare inode metadata, not contents; even a post-exit rehash would accept B consumed during the child followed by restoration of A.

A concrete execution passes the written checks: hash and header-bind expected archive A; overwrite the still-held inode with a trusted signed RPM B having the same NEVRA; verify and extract B; restore A before any after-check. The descriptor, dev, ino, size, retained sha256, selectionKey, and archiveDigest all describe A, signature verification succeeds on B, and authenticatedManifest is built from B.

cliInheritedFd.extractBytes also has no child-exit-zero, complete-cpio-trailer, no-trailing-data, or full-member-walk success rule. A partial rpm2cpio stream can be treated as authenticatedManifest even when extraction failed before a later duplicate-path or malformed member that the full archive rules would refuse.
blockers.impact: packagePayloadDigest and archive identity can remain bound to A while signature verification or authenticatedManifest comes from B. The resulting manifest can admit file-backed bytes or nominate a pathless kernel member that was never extracted from the signed archive digest in the observed authenticityCore.
blockers.requiredRepair: Snapshot publisherArchivePath once into an immutable byte object before headerBind. Use a sealed memfd or an equivalently enforced read-only snapshot with all writable handles closed and retained seal/immutability evidence; run headerBind, digest, verify, and extraction only on that snapshot. Require exact success/EOF for the selected extraction API, a complete cpio trailer with no unparsed trailing members on the CLI branch, and refusal on every read or extraction error. Descriptor identity is necessary but is not byte immutability.

blockers.title: The measured-boot record proves firmware LoadImage measurement but still has no evidence that StartImage transferred control to that kernel
evidence: kernelEvent retains a TCG_PCR_EVENT2/UEFI_IMAGE_LOAD_EVENT, its digest, eventData, and logIndex. That event proves a PE image was measured during LoadImage. It contains no StartImage result, EFI_HANDLE-to-StartImage association, or later control-transfer observation.

enforcedBootPolicy.controlTransfer requires StartImage of the same EFI_HANDLE, but no retained field, trusted probe, firmware transcript, or quote member observes that fact. Calling it a MUST does not make the unrecorded transition reproducible. The schema's UEFI_IMAGE_LOAD_EVENT bytes do not carry the asserted StartImage event.

Being pre-EV_SEPARATOR and having eventType EV_EFI_BOOT_SERVICES_APPLICATION does not authenticate the event's producer as the firmware LoadImage path. Pre-OS boot-service code can cause a matching pre-separator extend or can ask firmware to LoadImage approved K without ever starting K. The quote authenticates the resulting PCR extension sequence, not why the extension occurred or which bytes later received control.

A db-authorized boot application can therefore LoadImage the authenticated package member K, producing the exact event and PCR-4 digest v27 selects, then skip StartImage(K) and transfer control to M by its own loader/direct execution. PCR 7 still reports Secure Boot variables, PCR 4 and PCR 7 replay exactly, K's package and Authenticode signatures verify, the AK quote and fresh nonce verify, and every retained v27 value is identical to a lawful K boot.

The ceremony does not compare the other PCR-4 boot applications or firmware measurements to signed reference values and does not attest the measuring firmware itself. Secure Boot authenticates images admitted by db; it does not attest the behavior of an already-authorized boot component or turn a LoadImage event into proof of StartImage/control transfer.
blockers.impact: A machine can qualify the signed Linux OS-ABI member K while executing different kernel bytes M. This is the same executing-kernel false allow PTCB-V26-B2 required the successor to exclude; pre-separator filtering closes the stated post-separator attack but not the unobserved LoadImage-to-StartImage gap.
blockers.requiredRepair: Bind execution through an observable trusted handoff, not an asserted StartImage fact. Define and retain a firmware/boot-manager trust chain and boot-option/device-path ceremony that proves the selected direct boot target, validate every code-bearing component before the kernel against signed references, and include a trusted control-transfer measurement or attestation. Otherwise use a DRTM or enforced appraisal/measurement mechanism whose trusted policy proves the running kernel. The verifier must distinguish LoadImage(K)-then-run(M) from LoadImage(K)-then-StartImage(K).

blockers.title: RPM pathless events must retain a consumption record that the closed event schema explicitly forbids
evidence: preferredApi.retained unconditionally requires descriptorConsumptionRecord and cliInheritedFd.retained unconditionally requires materializedFileIdentity for the selected rpm-checksig acquisition branch. Those branches are used to produce packagePayloadDigest and authenticatedManifest for both file-backed and pathless RPM PLATFORM-ATTESTED events.

retainedEventSchema requires either record only when objectAuthenticityBindRecord is linux-file-backed and explicitly forbids both on linux-pathless. The extras-rejected linux-pathless tag contains neither record. Thus an RPM pathless event cannot both follow archiveAcquisition.retained and conform to the only closed retained event/tag schema.

OS ABI MUST use PATHLESS-PLATFORM-ATTESTED. rpm-checksig is the selected interface for amzn, fedora, rhel, sles, opensuse-leap, and opensuse-tumbleweed. Every such complete Linux profile therefore reaches the contradiction in its mandatory OS-ABI cell rather than merely an optional file-backed event.

For file-backed RPM events v27 places the same records twice: once as top-level retainedEventSchema members and again inside the extras-rejected linux-file-backed objectAuthenticityBindRecord. No rule selects one location or makes dir/name equal across the two copies. The newly nested associationToken fields also contradict openedObjectObservation's surviving statement that it is the only associationToken placement on this tag.
blockers.impact: RPM-family Linux OS-ABI profiles have no conforming retained trace even on a machine whose archive and measured boot otherwise pass. File-backed producers additionally have two incompatible evidence placements and can retain divergent copies. Linux remains slice 1, so this cannot be dismissed as a platform deferral.
blockers.requiredRepair: Choose exactly one location for each acquisition-consumption record, preferably one top-level conditional retained-event member. Require the selected record for every rpm-checksig event, including linux-pathless, and derive its associationToken from the containing runIdentity plus observedAt when no openedObjectObservation exists. Remove the duplicate nested fields and restore one associationToken placement. Keep branch mutual exclusion and archive/selection equalities in that single schema.

shouldFix.title: The stated PE/COFF image-digest procedure is a sequential file hash, not a complete Authenticode section-hash algorithm
evidence: v27 correctly separates flat member sha256 from peCoffImageDigest and excludes CheckSum, the Security data-directory entry, and the attribute certificate table. That closes the exact flat-preimage defect in CLAUDE-V26-B1.

The normative order then hashes the remainder sequentially in file order. It never parses SizeOfHeaders, IMAGE_SECTION_HEADER entries, PointerToRawData, or SizeOfRawData; never sorts sections by raw-file offset; and never defines overlap, gap, truncated-section, or overlay handling.

The referenced Windows Authenticode PE image hash hashes the headers and then section raw data under the section-table ordering/bounds rules before handling remaining data outside the certificate table. A valid PE with reordered raw sections, padding/gaps, or overlay data can therefore produce a firmware event digest different from v27's explicit procedure.

No PE32/PE32+ parser, offset-bound check, integer-overflow refusal, malformed certificate-table refusal, or test vector decides whether the external specification name or the conflicting abbreviated steps control.
shouldFix.impact: Some valid direct-boot EFI-stub kernels fail the central equality despite a correct firmware measurement, while validators can compute different peCoffImageDigest values for crafted or noncanonical PE layouts. The defect is fail-closed for ordinary mismatches but leaves the supposedly normative repair non-deterministic.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Specify the complete UEFI-compatible Authenticode image-hash algorithm: exact PE32/PE32+ parsing and bounds, SizeOfHeaders, checksum and Security-directory exclusions, section sorting by PointerToRawData, SizeOfRawData hashing, overlap/gap/overlay and certificate-table rules, and all malformed-input refusals. Pin the governing specification/version and include positive and adversarial digest test vectors.

shouldFix.title: The retained TPM quote, AK join, and nonce serialization still omit the operations needed for one reproducible verification
evidence: TPMS_ATTEST quote information contains a selected-PCR composite pcrDigest, not separate quoted PCR-4 and quoted PCR-7 values. replayAlgorithm says each reconstructed PCR MUST equal a quoted individual value, but no such values exist in the retained quote schema and no rule computes SHA-256(reconstructedPCR4 || reconstructedPCR7 in selection order) and compares it with attested.quote.pcrDigest.

quote.qualifiedSigner is a TPM2B_NAME, not a public verification key. akJoin says the signature verifies under that Name, but retains no TPMT_PUBLIC/AK public key, no certificate bytes, no Name derivation, and no equality from the derived AK Name to qualifiedSigner. The three-field akCertificateMember is also called a signed TCB member even though identityRuleShape.declared says every signed entry has four fields and a three-field form is nonconforming.

No explicit TPMS_ATTEST checks require TPM_GENERATED_VALUE magic, TPM_ST_ATTEST_QUOTE type, extraData byte equality to nonce, or the quoted pcrSelection/pcrDigest fields to equal the separately retained fields. Relying on the API name does not close the serialized verifier.

nonceBind uses u16be lengths but runIdentity, observedAt, and package name/version have no 65535-byte/digit cap or overflow refusal. 'subject canonical JSON' fixes key order but names no whitespace or JSON string-escaping rule, so equivalent producers can feed different bytes before the same fresh challenge.
shouldFix.impact: Independent validators cannot reproduce one quote verification or AK identity join, and long or differently escaped lawful identifiers have no defined nonce. Loose implementations can omit essential TPMS_ATTEST field checks; strict implementations may reject every record because the referenced individual PCR values and AK verification key are absent.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Define exact TPMS_ATTEST parsing and validation, compute the selected-bank PCR composite in TPM selection order, and compare it to the quote's pcrDigest. Retain the AK TPMT_PUBLIC and certificate bytes or an exact digest-bound reference to them, derive the TPM Name, compare it to qualifiedSigner, and verify TPMT_SIGNATURE with that public key. Use one conforming four-field signed-entry reference or define an explicitly named identity projection. Pin a canonical JSON serialization and either cap every u16-framed component with an explicit refusal or use a wider total length encoding.

verdictBasis: REJECT: 3 blockers and 2 SHOULD-FIX findings. ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.
conclusion: REJECT. v27 correctly separates flat and PE image digests, adds PCR 4/7 quote material and a fresh framed challenge, acquires a real publisher RPM, binds CLI children through /dev/fd/N, and unifies rpmHeaderIdentity. It still cannot distinguish measuring K from executing K, does not freeze RPM bytes while the held inode passes through digest/verify/extract, and forbids the required RPM consumption record on mandatory pathless events. The PE image-hash steps and TPM composite/AK/nonce verifier also remain incomplete. DR-126 remains OPEN; Linux remains D-002 slice 1; no DR is marked SATISFIED, and no D-096 (A) grant, sealing, application, or implementation authority is created.
